headline: Vapi is the branch furthest off target, and the gap starts with sales.
detail: Vapi booked ₹2.95 Cr in Jan–Sep 2026, 52% of its ₹5.68 Cr target, against 75% company-wide. It is also last on installation (46% of target) and has the fewest leads of any branch.

headline: Ahmedabad is the branch going backwards: agreement value is down 29% on last year.
detail: Ahmedabad booked ₹6.10 Cr in Jan–Sep 2026 against ₹8.55 Cr a year earlier, and it has the most AMC renewals due in the next 90 days (42).

headline: Pune leads on both sales (91% of target) and installation (97%).
detail: Company-wide, Jan–Sep 2026 agreement value is ₹28.30 Cr, down 2% on the same months of 2025, and 75% of the ₹37.68 Cr target.

headline: Service is a company-wide problem, not one branch's: 34% of 2026 repair orders missed SLA.
detail: Every branch breaches on more than one job in four (Surat worst at 38%, Vapi best at 29%). 90 repair orders are still open, 89 of them past SLA and 17 of them P1-Critical.

headline: Every branch misses somewhere: Surat on installation and service; Vadodara on sales, installation and service; Vapi on sales, installation and service; Ahmedabad on sales, installation and service; Pune on service.
detail: A branch is off target on sales below 85% of target, on installation below 85%, and on service above 25% of repair orders past SLA. Vadodara, Vapi and Ahmedabad miss on all three, so their gap is not one department's problem.

headline: Vapi's shortfall is lead volume, not conversion.
detail: Vapi generated 118 leads in Jan–Sep 2026, 55% of the branch average, yet converts 18.6% of leads into agreements, close to the company's 18.5%. More leads, not better closing, is the fix.

headline: Pune converts best because it wins more of its quotations.
detail: Lead-to-agreement conversion runs from 16.6% (Vadodara) to 21.8% (Pune). 40% of Pune's quotations become agreements, against 31% at Vadodara and Vapi.

headline: Cancelled and on-hold agreements hold ₹15.60 Cr of value.
detail: That is 12% of everything signed since 2023. On-hold deals (₹7.03 Cr) are the recoverable part and worth a monthly review.

headline: Architect referrals convert best (18.7%); cold calls convert worst (16.3%).
detail: The spread across sources is narrow. Source mix is not what separates strong and weak branches.

headline: Monthly bookings dipped from April to July 2026.
detail: April 2026 was the weakest of the last 24 complete months at ₹1.63 Cr. August and September recovered to ₹4.07 Cr and ₹4.82 Cr.

headline: Completions slowed in the second half while bookings held up, so the backlog is growing.
detail: Units completed fell from 44 a month in January–June to 29 a month in July–September, while new agreements added 45 units a month. 390 units on confirmed agreements are waiting or in work.

headline: 251 units are Delayed, and they tie up ₹6.06 Cr of open vendor POs.
detail: Delayed jobs take 57 days from start to finish against 40 for on-time jobs. Every open PO sits on a delayed or in-progress unit, so clearing delays also releases vendor cost.

headline: 207 'Pending' units belong to cancelled or on-hold agreements.
detail: They are not installation backlog. The dashboard shows them as parked so they do not inflate the backlog figure.

headline: Vapi's installation gap is mostly its sales gap carried forward.
detail: Vapi completed 37 units against a target of 81, with as many engineers as larger branches. Fewer agreements means fewer units to install. Its delayed share is 18%, the highest of any branch.

headline: Third-party cost is spread evenly: 15 vendors each take 6%–7% of PO value.
detail: No single vendor is a concentration risk. Total PO value to date is ₹27.92 Cr, about ₹1.9 L per unit across four line items.

headline: SLA breaches rose to 34% in Q3 2026, from 24% in Q4 2025.
detail: Repair volume is up as the installed base grows (118 ROs in Q3 2025, 129 in Q3 2026) without a matching gain in on-time closure. P1-Critical jobs breach as often as normal ones.

headline: 90 repair orders are still open, most of them for months.
detail: The median open RO is 246 days old and 17 are P1-Critical. Either the work is done and not closed in the system, or customers are waiting; both need a ticket-by-ticket review.

headline: 145 AMC contracts worth ₹1.33 Cr a year come up for renewal in the next 90 days.
detail: Ahmedabad has the most (42). Of contracts that have already expired, 25% were not followed by a new contract on the same unit.

headline: AMC capture after warranty is strong: 87% of out-of-warranty units have an active AMC.
detail: The active portfolio is 1,414 contracts worth ₹12.74 Cr a year, split almost evenly between comprehensive and non-comprehensive. 78 more units leave warranty in the next 90 days.

headline: Warranty jobs carry 82% of repair cost.
detail: 738 of 921 repair orders were on units under warranty, so the company absorbs most parts and labour cost. Cable wear is the most common fault (140 ROs). 248 units have needed two or more repairs.

headline: Targets for 4 of 8 roles are out of scale with the business.
detail: Company-wide attainment: Lead Generator 32%; Service Sales Person 911%; Service Supervisor 44%; Service Technician 13%. Attainment this far from 100% says the target was not built from the volume these teams handle. Reset them before tying incentives to them.

headline: 6 of 25 salespeople are at or above their Jan–Sep 2026 target.
detail: Individual attainment runs from 7% to 132%. The bottom five are a coaching list; the top five show what the plan allows.

headline: Incentives paid in Jan–Sep 2026 totalled ₹32.4 L, spread across all eight roles.
detail: Salespeople take the largest share. Payouts follow headcount more than results: branch totals ranged only from ₹5.8 L (Vapi) to ₹6.8 L (Ahmedabad), although sales attainment ranged from 52% to 91%.

headline: 346 incentive payments (₹20.0 L) are dated before the employee was hired.
detail: Listed with the other data issues below. Fix the source before using incentive history for pay decisions.
